basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Veneruntque duo angeli Sodomam vespere, sedente Lot in foribus civitatis. Non sine causa'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Veneruntque duo angeli Sodomam vespere, sedente Lot in foribus civitatis. Non sine causa angeli qui ad meridiem ad Abraham venerant, vespere Sodomam venire perhibentur, quia nimirum illi prospera ac laeta nuntiare, huic adversa inferre venerunt; ille fructu lucis ad coelestia flagrabat, haec vitiorum tenebris obsessa perditioni aeternae propinquabat.
